title: Post-Event Drift And Reversal
market_behavior: Prices may continue drifting or reverse after discrete events when attention, mandates, or information processing are slow.
forced_actor: Event-reactive funds, benchmark-aware holders, retail attention traders, and managers constrained by mandates or review cycles.
why_edge_might_exist: Markets may underreact or overreact to specific event categories when participants process information at different speeds.
why_large_capital_may_ignore_it: Clean event data is expensive and messy, effects can be crowded, and many events cannot absorb large capital after costs.
capacity_hypothesis: Capacity depends on event frequency and security liquidity; the attractive version is probably fragmented rather than one large universal event rule.
observable_predictions: Specific event cohorts show abnormal post-event drift or reversal after realistic costs.
The direction and holding period should be defined before looking at returns.
falsification_tests: Reject if event timestamps are not known before simulated entry.
Reject if the result disappears after conservative costs.
Weaken if only one event category or one date window works.
references: Academic literature on post-earnings announcement drift
